h1: Electric press brakes — servo-electric and ball-screw, 3 to 220 US tons
intro: An electric press brake drives the ram with servo motors and ball screws or belts instead of hydraulic cylinders: no oil, no pump running idle, ±0.01 mm repeatability, bending speeds to 30 mm/s and about 70 % less power — usually the better buy for 20 ga to 1/4″ sheet in a job shop, an enclosure or HVAC plant, or anywhere clean and quiet matters. NovoTech sells two lines in Canada, both on this page: the premium Dener DDM servo-electric press brakes from 44 to 220 US tons and 5 to 13 ft with the ESA S875 3D control, and the DDS ball-screw brakes of 22 and 44 tons for small parts; and NovoTech's own value-line electric press brakes, ball-screw driven, from 11 to 176 US tons and 1.6 to 10.5 ft with Delem control, plus 3 to 13 ton bench machines. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel and a 1-year warranty, installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For 3/8″ plate, tonnage above 220 tons or the lowest price per ton, see the hydraulic press brakes.

faq.q: Electric or hydraulic — which press brake should I buy?
faq.a: Electric when the work is sheet — 20 ga to 1/4″, brackets, enclosures, panels, stainless and aluminum — and when accuracy, speed, energy and a clean floor matter: the servo drive repeats to ±0.01 mm, bends at about twice the speed of a hydraulic brake and draws power only while the ram moves. Hydraulic when the work is plate, 3/8″ and up, long parts over 13 ft, or tonnage above 220 US tons, and when the lowest price per ton decides. Many shops run one of each; the hydraulic press brakes have their own page.

faq.q: Servo-electric or ball-screw — what is the difference?
faq.a: Both are electric. The DDM servo-electric brake drives the ram through servo motors and a belt-and-pulley system across the whole bending length, which is how it reaches 220 US tons and 13 ft with the force distributed evenly along the beam. The DDS and the value-line brakes drive the ram with two ball screws, one per side, each on its own servo motor — simpler, very accurate, and the right construction up to about 176 tons and 10 ft.

The premium DDM is built in Turkey by Dener with the 21″ ESA S875 W 3D control, 6-axis back gauges, laser angle measurement and robot cells as options, and Dener Canada parts in Mississauga, ON, Canada — the production electric brake. NovoTech's value-line electric brakes are built in China to our specification with Delem control and the same Estun servo components, at about two-thirds of the price — the electric brake for a job shop or a second machine for small parts. Both are installed and supported by the same NovoTech technicians.

faq.q: How much tonnage and length do I need?
faq.a: Air bending takes F = S² × 2 × R ÷ (1.4 × V) tonnes per metre of bend — the sheet thickness S and the V opening V in millimetres, the tensile strength R = 47 kg/mm² for mild steel (70 for stainless, 25 for aluminum), the formula behind the EUROSTAMP and Dener bending charts; in inches and US tons per foot it reads 575 × t² ÷ V. With the standard V of about 8 × the thickness, 3 mm needs about 24 t/m (8 US tons per foot), 6 mm 48 t/m (16), 1/4″ 54 t/m (18), 3/8″ in a 3″ V 80 t/m (27) and 1/2″ in a 5″ V 85 t/m (29). Multiply by the bend length and add about 20 % in reserve: 3 m × 6 mm is a 175-ton press brake, 10 ft × 1/4″ a 200 – 220 US ton machine, 10 ft × 3/8″ a 300 – 320 ton machine and 13 ft × 1/2″ a 400 – 450 ton machine. The tonnage calculator in the buying guide on the press brake page does the arithmetic for your thickness and length; tell us your thickest and longest bend and we size the brake and the tooling.

faq.q: What does an electric press brake cost to run?
faq.a: There is no hydraulic oil to buy, filter, cool or dispose of, no pump motor idling between bends, and the servo motors regenerate on the return stroke: Dener measures about 70 % less energy than a hydraulic brake of the same tonnage on sheet work, and the maintenance schedule is lubrication of the ball screws and guides. The machines are also quieter, which matters in a shop that runs the brake all day.

faq.q: What tooling fits, and do you stock it?
faq.a: The premium Dener and ISITAN brakes come with European-style (Promecam / Amada) quick-release clamping, and a sectioned punch set with a 2-V die ships with every machine of both lines; the value-line brakes use their own clamping, so tell us which tooling standard your shop already has and we fit the clamps to match. NovoTech stocks Eurostamp press brake tooling in Canada — punches, dies, radius, hemming and joggle tools, gooseneck and special profiles — and sizes it to your machine; Wila hydraulic clamping and American-style adapters are options.

faq.q: What about safety and the Ontario pre-start review?
faq.a: Side guards, an enclosed rear guard, interlocked doors and an anti-panic foot pedal with emergency stop are standard; DSP or Fiessler laser finger protection and light curtains are options we recommend for every CNC machine. In Ontario a new press brake needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs.

faq.q: Do you deliver, install and service in Canada?
faq.a: Yes — NovoTech delivers across Canada and the United States from Mississauga, ON, Canada, commissions the machine and trains your operators — free of charge in the Greater Toronto Area, on request elsewhere; Dener Canada and NovoTech stock the parts here. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, 600 V standard (208 / 240 / 480 V on request), a 1-year warranty and remote diagnostics through the control.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
